arxiv-1604-03610.title: Uniform Value for Recursive Games with Compact Actions
arxiv-1604-03610.creator: Xiaoxi Li, Sylvain Sorin
arxiv-1604-03610.description: Abstract Mertens, Neyman and Rosenberg [ 6 ] used the Mertens and Neyman theorem [ 5 ] to prove the existence of uniform value for absorbing games with finite state space and compact action sets. We provide an analogous proof for another class of stochastic games, recursive games with finite state space and compact action sets.

arxiv-1605-07192.title: Underlying event sensitive observables in Drell-Yan production using GENEVA Journal: Eur. Phys. J. C
arxiv-1605-07192.creator: Simone Alioli e1,addr1, Christian W. Bauer e2,addr2, Sam Guns e3,addr2, Frank J. Tackmann e4,addr3
arxiv-1605-07192.description: A 2016 arXiv research paper by Simone Alioli e1,addr1, Christian W. Bauer e2,addr2, Sam Guns e3,addr2, Frank J. Tackmann e4,addr3. We present an extension of the Geneva Monte Carlo framework to include multiple parton interactions (MPI) provided by Pythia8 . This allows us to obtain predictions for underlying-event sensitive measurements in Drell-Yan production, in conjunction with Geneva ’s fully-differential NNLO \mathrm{NNLO} calculation, NNLL ′ \mathrm{NNLL}^{\prime} resummation for the 0-jet resolution variable (beam thrust), and NLL \mathrm{NLL} resummation for the 1 1 -jet resolution variable.

arxiv-2108-13851.title: Electronic States and Anomalous Hall Effect in Strongly Correlated Topological Systems
arxiv-2108-13851.creator: Valentin Yu. Irkhin, Yuri N. Skryabin
arxiv-2108-13851.description: Abstract We treat elementary excitations, the spin-liquid state, and the anomalous Hall effect (including the quantum one in purely 2D situation) in layered highly correlated systems. The mechanisms of the formation of a topological state associated with bare flat energy bands, correlations, and spin-orbit interactions, including the appearance of correlated Chern bands, are analyzed.

arxiv-2205-03698.title: Embedding of Higson compactification into the product of adelic solenoids. Thanks: The first author was supported by Simons Foundation
arxiv-2205-03698.creator: Alexander Dranishnikov, James Keesling
arxiv-2205-03698.description: Abstract . The Higson compactification of any simply connected proper geodesic metric space admits an embedding into a product of adelic solenoids that induces an isomorphism of 1-dimensional cohomology. 2000 Mathematics Subject Classification Primary 53C23, 54F15; Secondary 22C05, 54F15, 55N05 1.

arxiv-2209-00035.title: Relative entropy of an interval for a massless boson at finite temperature
arxiv-2209-00035.creator: Alan Garbarz, Gabriel Palau
arxiv-2209-00035.description: Abstract We compute Araki’s relative entropy associated to a bounded interval I = ( a , b ) I=(a,b) between a thermal state and a coherent excitation of itself in the bosonic U(1)-current model, namely the (derivative of the) chiral boson.

arxiv-2302-02912.title: The interactions of the elliptical instability and convection
arxiv-2302-02912.creator: Nils B. de Vries, Adrian J. Barker, Rainer Hollerbach
arxiv-2302-02912.description: Abstract The elliptical instability is an instability of elliptical streamlines, which can be excited by large-scale tidal flows in rotating fluid bodies, and excites inertial waves if the dimensionless tidal amplitude ( ϵ \epsilon ) is sufficiently large. It operates in convection zones but its interactions with turbulent convection have not been studied in this context.

arxiv-2307-14587.title: Artificial intelligence-aided protein engineering: from topological data analysis to deep protein language models
arxiv-2307-14587.creator: Yuchi Qiu, Guo-Wei Wei, Yuchi Qiu, Guo-Wei Wei
arxiv-2307-14587.description: Abstract Protein engineering is an emerging field in biotechnology that has the potential to revolutionize various areas, such as antibody design, drug discovery, food security, ecology, and more. However, the mutational space involved is too vast to be handled through experimental means alone.

arxiv-2308-04721.title: Linear shrinkage of sample covariance matrix or matrices under elliptical distributions: a review
arxiv-2308-04721.creator: Esa Ollila
arxiv-2308-04721.description: Abstract This chapter reviews methods for linear shrinkage of the sample covariance matrix (SCM) and matrices (SCM-s) under elliptical distributions in single and multiple populations settings, respectively. In the single sample setting a popular linear shrinkage estimator is defined as a linear combination of the sample covariance matrix (SCM) with a scaled identity matrix.

arxiv-2405-05845.title: Non-Binary Covering Codes for Low-Access Computations Thanks: Parts of this work were done when V. Ramkumar was a visiting researcher in the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Washington University in St. Louis. The work of V. Ramkumar and I. Tamo was supported by the European Research
arxiv-2405-05845.creator: Vinayak Ramkumar †, Netanel Raviv ⋆, Itzhak Tamo †
arxiv-2405-05845.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Vinayak Ramkumar †, Netanel Raviv ⋆, Itzhak Tamo †. Given a real dataset and a computation family, we wish to encode and store the dataset in a distributed system so that any computation from the family can be performed by accessing a small number of nodes. In this work, we focus on the families of linear computations where the coefficients are restricted to a finite set of real values.

arxiv-2406-08603.title: FakeInversion: Learning to Detect Images from Unseen Text-to-Image Models by Inverting Stable Diffusion
arxiv-2406-08603.creator: George Cazenavette 1 Avneesh Sud 2 Thomas Leung 2 Ben Usman 2 1 Massachusetts Institute of Technology 2 Google Research fake-inversion.github.io
arxiv-2406-08603.description: Abstract Due to the high potential for abuse of GenAI systems, the task of detecting synthetic images has recently become of great interest to the research community. Unfortunately, existing image-space detectors quickly become obsolete as new high-fidelity text-to-image models are developed at blinding speed.

arxiv-2410-05722.title: A Novel Low-Complexity Peak-Power-Assisted Data-Aided Channel Estimation Scheme for MIMO-OFDM Wireless Systems
arxiv-2410-05722.creator: INAAMULLAH KHAN, MOHAMMAD MAHMUDUL HASAN, AND MICHAEL CHEFFENA
arxiv-2410-05722.description: Abstract This paper, for the first time, presents a low-complexity peak-power-assisted data-aided channel estimation (DACE) scheme for both single-input single-output (SISO) and multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) wireless systems. In OFDM, high peak-power levels occur when the subcarriers align in phase and constructively interfere with each other.

arxiv-2501-08928.title: Formulas as Processes, Deadlock-Freedom as Choreographies (Extended Version)
arxiv-2501-08928.creator: Matteo Acclavio, Giulia Manara, Fabrizio Montesi
arxiv-2501-08928.description: Abstract We introduce a novel approach to studying properties of processes in the π \pi -calculus based on a processes-as-formulas interpretation, by establishing a correspondence between specific sequent calculus derivations and computation trees in the reduction semantics of the recursion-free π \pi -calculus.

arxiv-2503-19797.title: Fail Faster
arxiv-2503-19797.creator: Cynthia Richey, Joseph W. Cutler, Harrison Goldstein, Benjamin C. Pierce
arxiv-2503-19797.description: Abstract . Property-based testing (PBT) relies on generators for random test cases, often constructed using embedded domain specific languages, which provide expressive combinators for building and composing generators. The effectiveness of PBT depends critically on the speed of these generators.

arxiv-2504-03274.title: Do Large Language Models Solve the Problems of Agent-Based Modeling? A Critical Review of Generative Social Simulations
arxiv-2504-03274.creator: Maik Larooij, Petter Törnberg
arxiv-2504-03274.description: Abstract Recent advancements in AI have reinvigorated Agent-Based Models (ABMs), as the integration of Large Language Models (LLMs) has led to the emergence of “generative ABMs” as a novel approach to simulating social systems. While ABMs offer means to bridge micro-level interactions with macro-level patterns, they have long faced criticisms from social scientists, pointing to e.g.

arxiv-2510-16976.creator: Daniele Sepe, Susan Tolman
arxiv-2510-16976.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Daniele Sepe, Susan Tolman. In an earlier paper, we proved the connectedness of the fibers of every 2 ​ n 2n -dimensional integrable system satisfying both: (A) the action extends the action of an ( n − 1 ) (n-1) -dimensional torus which has a proper moment map, and (B) every tall singular point is non-degenerate and no such point has a hyperbolic block and connected T T -stabilizer. Unfortunately, these criteria are fairly restrictive.

plos-pone-0002144.creator: Deborah French, Wenjian Yang, Leo H. Hamilton et al.
plos-pone-0002144.description: PLOS ONE research article. The degree to which gene expression covaries between different primary tissues within an individual is not well defined. We hypothesized that expression that is concordant across tissues is more likely influenced by genetic variability than gene expression which is discordant bet

pmc-10571369.title: What we should consider to facilitate recovery of the hematological profile in all patients after pancreaticoduodenectomy: the role of preoperative intravenous iron treatment
pmc-10571369.creator: Eun Young Kim, Sung Eun Park, Tae Ho Hong
pmc-10571369.description: BackgroundIn pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD), the duodenum and upper jejunum responsible for iron absorption are removed, which can lead to massive hemorrhage during surgery and cause iron deficiency anemia after PD. The aim of this study was to evaluate overall changes in hematologic profiles of patients who underwent pancreaticoduodenectomy.

pmc-10692374.title: Integrative approach to lifestyle management: Implications for public health research & practice in the context of SDG-3
pmc-10692374.creator: Krishnamurthy Jayanna
pmc-10692374.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). In the last 100 years, the communicable diseases have been replaced by non-communicable diseases as the leading cause of deaths across the world. Periodically, the communicable disease outbreaks continue to pose a challenge to the public health systems. Change in human behaviors and lifestyles are recognized as risk factors for the public health challenges we face today, which significantly affect wellbeing and quality of life. Healthy lifestyles are critical to not only controlling diseases, but also to promote good health and wellbeing.

pmc-11715838.title: Investigating Spatial Characteristics of Brain Atrophy in Alzheimer’s and LATE neuropathology
pmc-11715838.creator: Khalid Saifullah, Abdur Raquib Ridwan, David A Bennett, Julie A Schneider, Konstantinos Arfanakis
pmc-11715838.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundAlzheimer’s disease neuropathologic change (AD‐NC) and limbic‐predominant age‐related TDP‐43 encephalopathy neuropathologic change (LATE‐NC) are common in older adults and have been associated with brain atrophy, cognitive decline, and dementia. Since AD‐NC and LATE‐NC are often comorbid and due to the fact that LATE‐NC can only be detected at autopsy, in this work, we combined deformation‐based morphometry (DBM) on ex‐vivo brain MRI and detailed neuropathological evaluation in a large number of community‐based older adults to investigate the difference in brain atrophy patterns associated

pmc-12399378.title: Human papillomavirus, human immunodeficiency virus, and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma in South Africa: a study of prevalence, co-infection, and risk factors
pmc-12399378.creator: Sikhumbuzo Z. Mbatha, Tania Maphosho, Dakalo Ramali, Botle Damane, Portia Nevhungoni, Michelle Mc-Cabe, Benny Mosoane, Rodney Hull, Zodwa Dlamini
pmc-12399378.description: BackgroundEsophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) is a serious public health concern in South Africa, ranking among the most lethal malignancies. It has known risk factors including human papillomavirus (HPV). HPV is strongly linked to squamous cell cancers (i.e., cervix, anus, and oropharynx) with human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) shown to increase susceptibility to HPV-related malignancies.

pmc-12489077.title: Energy efficient traffic data aggregation and routing for metropolitan optical access network
pmc-12489077.creator: T. Senthil Kumar, Mohan. V, S. Senthilkumar
pmc-12489077.description: The Energy Efficient Regional Area Metropolitan Optical Access Network (MOAN) is a modern optical communication system specifically designed for metropolitan areas. It addresses the increasing demand for high-speed data transmission while optimizing energy consumption. In this paper, energy-efficient traffic data aggregation and energy-aware routing are presented to increase the network lifetime of the system.

pmc-12512368.title: Improving racial data equity among minority groups in South Carolina using COVID-19 as an example: application of principal components analysis
pmc-12512368.creator: FNU Rubaiya, Janet O’Connor, Lyubomir N. Kolev, James M. Antill, Margaret Iiams, LaNaya A. Martin, Chantaezia Z. Joseph, Claire Youngblood, Jennifer Almeda-Garrett, Linda E. Kelemen
pmc-12512368.description: BackgroundData inequity occurs when racial and ethnic groups are aggregated during data collection or reporting despite their differences. To demonstrate racial data equity importance, we re-analyzed South Carolina’s (SC) census data and COVID-19 case-rate and death-rate distributions according to age, sex, and new combined single and multiracial categories.

pmc-13228178.title: Antihypertensive drugs and arteriovenous fistula flow rates among patients on maintenance hemodialysis in Egypt
pmc-13228178.creator: Enass Elsayed, Khaled M. Kotb, Mohamed Abdel-Salam El-Awady, Manar Samy M., Omnia Ali, Mohammed Abdel Gawad
pmc-13228178.description: Vascular access dysfunction is a major cause of morbidity among maintenance hemodialysis (HD) patients. Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) may affect vascular remodeling; however, their impact on arteriovenous fistula (AVF) flow rate remains uncertain. We evaluated the association between antihypertensive therapy, particularly CCBs, and AVF flow rate in maintenance HD patients.

pmc-13284697.title: Generative AI in higher education: a meta-analysis of intellectual and social–emotional outcomes
pmc-13284697.creator: Chunai Liu, Lidong Xie, Gang Xu
pmc-13284697.description: BackgroundGenerative AI has rapidly entered higher education, yet evidence on its effects across learning domains remains fragmented. This study synthesized experimental evidence on whether generative AI improves intellectual outcomes and social emotional outcomes among higher education students.MethodsA systematic review and meta-analysis was conducted on 33 experimental and quasi-experimental studies involving 3,394 participants.

pmc-13334222.title: A Synergistic Dual‐Antibody Cocktail Targeting α‐Toxin Protects Against Invasive Staphylococcus aureus Infection by Neutralizing Virulence and Enhancing Host Defense
pmc-13334222.creator: Liqun Zhao, Zhen Song, Hongyin Fan, Lei Wang, Yun Yang, Haiming Jing, Xin Xia, Yu Wang, Leilei Feng, Sheng Wang, Zhifu Chen, Qiang Gou, Yue Yuan, Jinyong Zhang, Quanming Zou, Hao Zeng
pmc-13334222.description: Staphylococcus aureus is a leading cause of severe invasive infections and is associated with high mortality. The pore‐forming α‐toxin (Hla) is a key virulence determinant that drives disease severity. We identified two high‐affinity anti‐Hla monoclonal antibodies, Hm0399 and Hm0411, derived from the sera of volunteers vaccinated with the S. aureus vaccine rFSAV.

pmc-13350116.title: Modality-dependent bottom-up attention and eye gaze direction affect auditory spatial discrimination
pmc-13350116.creator: René Šebeňa, Jyrki Ahveninen, Virginia Best, Barbara Shinn-Cunningham, Norbert Kopčo
pmc-13350116.description: AbstractA combined behavioral and EEG experiment examined the effects of intramodal and crossmodal cueing on auditory spatial discrimination. On each trial, the participant fixated a neutral location and was presented with an auditory target (two broadband “buzzes” with a slight relative spatial offset) from one of two locations (central or lateral).

pmc-13375870.title: Integrative analysis of the metabolome and transcriptome reveals the mechanism of flower color and antioxidant capacity in three Syringa cultivars
pmc-13375870.creator: Hailiang Zhang, Xiaofei Wang, Siting Wang, Zhiying Yang, Huayang Li, Meng Li, Xiaoyu Zhang, Xuekai Gao, YueBo Sun, Kezhong Zhang, Ruidong Han, Qingzhu Zhao, Shuhua Yang
pmc-13375870.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Lilac plants (Syringa spp.) are extensively valued in landscaping and human health for their colorful cultivars and significantly medicinal and edible properties. The current works mainly focus on the anthocyanidin-induced pigmentation or the flavonoid-driven antioxidant activity, respectively. Nevertheless, the genetic and metabolic panorama of flavonoids, especially the metabolic flux partitioning of anthocyanidin and other flavonoids, remains ambiguous in the Syringa vulgaris plants.
